Pexels · 6864751
Welcoming the Lunar New Year
The decision to welcome the new year together may appear ordinary, yet it exposes a recurring tension between arrangements that
make life manageable and experiences that resist being prescribed. A defensible approach combines proportionate preparation with a
willingness to reconsider whose interests a plan serves.
Preparation has value because asking about a custom prevents careless assumptions. In the present case, we ask the host how their
family exchanges greetings. Such an intervention is modest, but that modesty is its strength: it removes a foreseeable obstacle
without claiming to determine the entire experience. Structure is useful to the extent that it releases attention rather than consuming
it.
That argument requires a qualification, however: sharing time connects generations. For instance, we invite an older relative to
explain a family recipe. An arrangement that appears efficient from one standpoint may impose costs elsewhere. Listening to those
affected is therefore not an optional gesture of goodwill; it supplies information without which the plan cannot be adequately evaluated.
The resulting principle is one of proportion. Preparation deserves support when it clarifies responsibilities and protects time, while
responsiveness prevents it from hardening into an end in itself. To judge the experience well is to examine both what the arrangement
enables and what it may inadvertently exclude.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete example.
Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write about an
experience of your own.
Explain the meaning before looking at the model answer. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example.
